Proposed model involves the overexpression of ZmPEPC, GmAspAT and NtGS in Brassica, aiming to utilize more CO2 and NH3 for primary and secondary metabolite biosynthesis and increased biomass production as identified by NMR

A proposed model involves the overexpression of ZmPEPC, GmAspAT and NtGS in Brassica, aiming to utilize more CO2 and NH3 for primary and secondary metabolite biosynthesis and increased biomass production as identified by NMR. Transgenic plants coexpressing ZmPEPC, GmAspAT and NtGS enhance CO2 and NH3 utilization, channelling them towards primary and secondary metabolites. Enhanced PEPC activity produces OAA, facilitating Asp synthesis using Glu as an ammonia source. Higher GS activity ensures a higher NH3 assimilation rate and Glu synthesis via the GS‐GOGAT pathway. The Krebs cycle connects carbon source utilization and NH3 assimilation through α‐ketoglutarate, central to C and N metabolism. PAG coexpression increases C utilization for carbohydrate (glucose, fructose, sucrose) and amino acid synthesis (alanine, aspartate, methionine, cysteine, glutamine, proline, arginine, glycine, serine). Increased CO2 utilization enhances glucose production and sucrose synthesis, metabolized by invertases and SuSy enzymes, releasing hexose phosphates for the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway, providing acetyl‐CoA for fatty acid production. Pyruvate kinase directs carbon partitioning towards protein and oil accumulation pathways. Higher aspartate levels indicate CO2 utilization towards aspartate family amino acids, methionine regulating important metabolites. Photorespiratory C may also be exported from the photorespiratory pathway in the form of the amino acid glycine and serine, or as CH2‐THF and o‐acetylserine. CH2‐THF supplies one‐carbon (C1) units to the C1 metabolism and synthesis of o‐acetylserine by SAT3 draws from the serine pool in the mitochondria for cystine synthesis which is the merging point of C, N and S metabolism. CO2 and NH3 utilization also channel into the shikimic acid pathway for aromatic amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. The overexpressed enzymes PEPC, AspAT and GS were represented by red arrows. The metabolites found to be higher in PAG‐coexpressing lines were represented by yellow and grey boxes with red arrows. 2PG, 2‐phosphoglycolate; 3PG, 3‐phosphoglycerate; ADPG, ADP‐glucose; Asp, aspartic acid; AspAT, aspartate aminotransferase; CH2‐THF, methyltetrahydrofolate; DAHP, 3‐deoxy‐D‐arabino‐heptulosonate‐7‐phosphate; FRK, fructokinase; GDC, glycine decarboxylase; Gln, glutamine; Glu, glutamate; GOGAT, glutamate‐oxoglutarate aminotransferase; GS, glutamine synthetase; HXK, hexokinase; Inv, invertases; OAA, oxaloacetic acid; OAS‐TL, o‐acetylserine(thiol)lyase; PEPC, phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase; PEP, phosphoenolpyruvate; PKP, pyruvate kinase; SAT, serine acetyltransferase; SHMT, serine hydroxymethyltransferase; SuSy, sucrose synthases
